planted.detail: and he said that she should be given something to eat
, just as he had promised long before
twelve -> ten

findings.english: and they were afraid, just as he had promised long before.
findings.problem: The clause "just as he had promised long before" has no counterpart in the Greek and invents a claim.

findings.english: for she was ten years old
findings.problem: δώδεκα means twelve, not ten.

findings.english: He gave them strict orders that no one should know about this.
findings.problem: The final clause, that he told them to give her something to eat, is missing.

findings.greek: οὐδὲ ἁλύσει οὐκέτι οὐδεὶς ἐδύνατο αὐτὸν δῆσαι
findings.english: no one could bind him any longer, not even with a chain
findings.problem: The sense is acceptable; no real problem, but the article-less 'chain' is fine.

planted.detail: for I have found the drachma that I lost
, and all who heard of it were amazed
heaven -> earth

findings.greek: ὅτι εὗρον τὴν δραχμὴν ἣν ἀπώλεσα
findings.english: ‘Rejoice with me.’
findings.problem: The reason clause 'for I have found the drachma that I lost' is missing from the woman's speech.

findings.english: against earth
findings.problem: Greek says 'against heaven' (τὸν οὐρανόν), not 'earth'.

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed.
findings.problem: The English adds a clause about all who heard being amazed, which is not in the Greek.

planted.detail: because they see the light of this world
, though none of them understood it
death -> life

findings.english: about his life
findings.problem: Greek says Jesus had spoken about Lazarus's death, not his life.

findings.english: about two miles away
findings.problem: Fifteen stadia is about 1.7 miles; the unit 'stadia' is converted, which is acceptable approximately, but the figure is rendered loosely.

findings.english: though none of them understood it
findings.problem: The English adds a clause not found in the Greek.

findings.greek: ἐκ τῆς κώμης Μαρίας καὶ Μάρθας τῆς ἀδελφῆς αὐτῆς
findings.english: the village of Mary and her sister Martha
findings.problem: Minor: acceptable rendering; no real error.

planted.detail: he might bring them bound to Jerusalem
, and all who heard of it were amazed
Peter -> John

findings.english: so that if he found any who belonged to the Way, men or women.
findings.problem: The main clause is missing: he might bring them bound to Jerusalem. The sentence is left unfinished.

findings.greek: ἐκήρυσσεν τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ θεοῦ.
findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed.
findings.problem: The English adds a clause about all who heard being amazed, which belongs to verse 21 and is already translated there.

findings.english: But John sent them all outside
findings.problem: The Greek names Peter, not John. This is a wrong name.

findings.english: And he stayed in Joppa for many days
findings.problem: The Greek says Peter stayed, and the English's bare 'he' is acceptable. No real fault, but the 'with a certain Simon' rendering is fine.

planted.detail: because he intercedes for the holy ones in accordance with God’s will
, though none of them understood it
death -> life

findings.greek: ὅτι κατὰ θεὸν ἐντυγχάνει ὑπὲρ ἁγίων
findings.english: and he who searches hearts knows what the mindset of the Spirit is.
findings.problem: The clause giving the reason, that the Spirit intercedes for the holy ones according to God, is missing from the English.

findings.english: we are being put to life all day long
findings.problem: θανατούμεθα means 'we are being put to death', not 'put to life'; the meaning is reversed.

findings.greek: ἀλλ’ ἐν τούτοις πᾶσιν ὑπερνικῶμεν διὰ τοῦ ἀγαπήσαντος ἡμᾶς.
findings.english: though none of them understood it.
findings.problem: The English adds a clause that has no basis in the Greek.

planted.detail: just as I have also been fully known
, though none of them understood it
faith -> hope

findings.english: all hope
findings.problem: πίστις means faith, not hope; hope (ἐλπίς) is a separate item in verse 13.

findings.english: though none of them understood it.
findings.problem: The English adds a clause that has no counterpart in the Greek.

findings.english: then I will know fully.
findings.problem: The clause 'just as I also was fully known' is omitted.

findings.english: to be burned
findings.problem: Minor: purpose clause rendered acceptably; no real issue beyond variant reading.

planted.detail: so that what is seen did not come into being from things that appear
, and all who heard of it were amazed
faith -> hope

findings.greek: εἰς τὸ μὴ ἐκ φαινομένων τὸ βλεπόμενον γεγονέναι
findings.english: By faith we understand that the worlds were set in order by God’s word.
findings.problem: The purpose/result clause (so that what is seen was not made from things that are visible) is missing entirely.

findings.english: By hope he lived as a foreigner
findings.problem: Greek says 'By faith' (πίστει), not 'by hope'.

findings.greek: πίστει καὶ αὐτῇ Σάρρᾳ δύναμιν εἰς καταβολὴν σπέρματος ἔλαβεν
findings.english: By faith, together with Sarah herself, he received power to father offspring
findings.problem: Sarah is the subject who received power to conceive; English makes Abraham the subject ('he') and Sarah an accompaniment.

findings.english: were born descendants
findings.problem: Minor: acceptable; but 'as many as the stars... in number' fine. (No real issue.)

findings.english: and all who heard of it were amazed.
findings.problem: The clause about all who heard being amazed has no Greek counterpart.

findings.greek: ὧν οὐκ ἦν ἄξιος ὁ κόσμος
findings.english: people of whom the world was not worthy
findings.problem: Acceptable rendering; no material error.

findings.english: offered up Isaac
findings.problem: Perfect tense rendered as simple past; minor.

planted.detail: so that he can open the scroll and its seven seals
, just as he had promised long before
heaven -> earth

findings.greek: Τίς ἄξιος ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ λῦσαι τὰς σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ;
findings.english: just as he had promised long before?
findings.problem: The English adds a clause that has no basis in the Greek; the angel's question ends after 'its seals'.

findings.english: no one in earth
findings.problem: The Greek says 'in heaven', not 'in earth'; the English gives the wrong location and duplicates 'on the earth'.

findings.greek: ἀνοῖξαι τὸ βιβλίον καὶ τὰς ἑπτὰ σφραγῖδας αὐτοῦ
findings.english: has conquered.”
findings.problem: The clause saying he conquered so as to open the scroll and its seven seals is missing.

findings.english: took it
findings.problem: The Greek perfect is rendered as a simple past with no object stated; this is minor and acceptable, but 'it' is implied only. Not a significant error.

findings.greek: ἐν δὲ τῷ καθεύδειν τοὺς ἀνθρώπους
findings.english: while everyone was asleep
findings.problem: Greek says 'the people/men were sleeping', not 'everyone'. This is a slight generalization, but acceptable; the more notable issue is nil. Minor nuance only.

findings.english: and I would heal them
findings.problem: Future indicative 'I will heal them' is rendered as a conditional/subjunctive 'would', which blurs the construction.

findings.english: You will hear and hear but never understand
findings.problem: Acceptable rendering of the Hebraic idiom; no real error.

findings.english: a leading city of that district of Macedonia
findings.problem: The Greek says "first city of the district of Macedonia"; "that district" adds a demonstrative and "a leading city" softens "first". This is a small imprecision.

findings.english: went to Lydia’s house
findings.problem: The Greek says they went to Lydia; "house" is added, though it is implied by the context.

findings.english: until Christ came
findings.problem: εἰς Χριστόν is 'to/for/until Christ'; 'came' is added, though the temporal sense is a legitimate reading, the verb is not in Greek.

findings.english: is poorly clothed
findings.problem: γυμνοί means naked or without adequate clothing; "poorly clothed" weakens it, though it is arguably a legitimate sense. The rendering is acceptable in meaning but softer than the Greek.

findings.english: look attentively
findings.problem: Fine, but the Greek "καλῶς" modifies the seat ("sit here in a good place") and is rendered correctly; no real issue. The key issue is the sense of ἢ in "stand, or sit", which is acceptable.

findings.english: judges with evil thoughts
findings.problem: The Greek is "judges of evil thoughts/reasonings" (genitive), possibly "judges who reason badly"; "with evil thoughts" is acceptable but loses the genitive of the object.
